preconditions.description: The number of nodes n is between 1 and 100,000 inclusive.
The number of edges m is between 1 and 100,000 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= u_i <= n and 1 <= v_i <= n for u_i, v_i in edges)
preconditions.description: Each edge connects nodes within the range 1 to n inclusive.

postconditions.description: The output sequence contains exactly n nodes.
The output sequence contains each node from 1 to n exactly once.
The output sequence starts with node 1.

postconditions.expression: all(int(return_value.split()[i]) in [int(u) for u, v in edges if int(return_value.split()[i-1]) == u or int(return_value.split()[i-1]) == v] for i in range(1, n))
postconditions.description: Each node in the output sequence is connected to the previous node by an edge.

postconditions.expression: return_value == min([' '.join(map(str, perm)) for perm in permutations(range(1, n+1)) if ' '.join(map(str, perm)).split()[0] == '1' and all(int(' '.join(map(str, perm)).split()[i]) in [int(u) for u, v in edges if int(' '.join(map(str, perm)).split()[i-1]) == u or int(' '.join(map(str, perm)).split()[i-1]) == v] for i in range(1, n))])
postconditions.description: The output sequence is the lexicographically smallest valid sequence of nodes.
